issues.legal_issue: An agreement to construct a unit for a purchaser before construction is complete constitutes a works contract, and the transfer of goods involved in that construction is taxable.
material_facts: The developer entered into agreements with prospective purchasers before construction was complete.
Under the agreements, the developer undertook to construct units for purchasers in return for consideration payable in instalments.
The agreements provided for purchasers to acquire units and an undivided interest in the land.
The tax authorities assessed tax on the transfer of property in goods involved in the construction.
issues.conclusion: Construction undertaken for purchasers under agreements made before completion is a works contract, and tax is payable on the turnover of goods transferred in its execution. An agreement made after the unit is already constructed does not constitute a works contract.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(1)(v-i), 2(1)(k)(viii) and 5B of the Karnataka Sales Tax Act, a works contract broadly includes any agreement for construction for cash, deferred payment or other valuable consideration; it is not limited to the conventional meaning of work performed for another. Tax under section 5B applies to the taxable turnover of property in goods transferred in executing such a contract. The Karnataka Ownership Flats Act does not determine whether an agreement is a works contract for this purpose.

rule.if: sales_tax_assessment_appeal and agreement_precedes_completion and construction_for_purchaser and consideration_for_construction and goods_transferred_in_construction

predicates.sales_tax_assessment_appeal: The proceeding concerns an appeal from a sales tax assessment relating to construction activity.
predicates.agreement_precedes_completion: The construction agreement was made before the unit was fully constructed.
predicates.construction_for_purchaser: The developer undertook under the agreement to construct the unit for a purchaser.
predicates.consideration_for_construction: The purchaser agreed to provide cash, deferred payment or other valuable consideration for the construction.
predicates.goods_transferred_in_construction: Property in goods was transferred in the course of carrying out the construction.

issues.definition: When a tax assessment appeal concerns goods transferred in construction for a purchaser under a pre-completion agreement for consideration, the turnover of those goods is taxable.

issues.legal_issue: A developer's claimed ownership of the property does not prevent construction for purchasers from being treated as a works contract.
material_facts: The developer relied on its development agreement, possession and rights over the property to claim ownership despite having no registered conveyance.
The purchaser agreements described the developer as constructing units for purchasers for consideration.
The developer argued that an owner could not perform a works contract on behalf of another.
issues.conclusion: Ownership does not exclude a construction agreement from the definition of a works contract; even an owner may undertake a works contract by agreeing to construct for another for consideration. The developer's claimed rights did not make it the owner for purposes of the sales tax legislation, and the court did not need to decide ownership to determine whether the agreements were works contracts.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(1)(v-i), 2(1)(k)(viii) and 5B of the Karnataka Sales Tax Act focus on the agreement to construct for consideration and the transfer of goods in its execution, not on whether the contractor owns the property. The interpretation of ownership in CIT v. Podar Cement Ltd. and Mysore Minerals Ltd. was made in the context of the Income Tax Act and did not assist in determining ownership under the Karnataka Sales Tax Act; possession and a right to construct without a registered conveyance did not establish ownership in this context.

predicates.sales_tax_assessment_appeal: The proceeding concerns an appeal from a sales tax assessment relating to construction activity.
predicates.construction_for_another: A person undertook to construct property for someone else under an agreement.
predicates.consideration_for_construction: The person undertaking construction was to receive cash, deferred payment or other valuable consideration.

issues.definition: If a person undertakes construction for someone else for consideration in a sales tax assessment appeal, the person's ownership of the property does not prevent the agreement from being a works contract.

issues.legal_issue: A contractual right to terminate an agreement and forfeit part of the purchaser's payments does not by itself prevent the agreement from being a works contract.
material_facts: The purchaser agreements allowed the developer to terminate for breach and forfeit part of the payments made.
The agreements also allowed the developer, upon termination, to dispose of the unit elsewhere.
The court distinguished a terminated agreement where the unit was retained from an agreement that remained in force.
issues.conclusion: A termination and forfeiture clause does not by itself change the character of an otherwise qualifying works contract. While the agreement remains in force, construction is for the purchaser; if the agreement is terminated and the unit is retained by the developer, there is no works contract to that extent.
issues.legal_principle: The definition in section 2(1)(v-i) of the Karnataka Sales Tax Act turns on the agreement to construct for consideration. A contractual power to terminate does not negate that agreement while it remains in force, but where termination occurs and the unit is retained rather than built for a purchaser, the construction is not for that purchaser under a subsisting agreement.

rule.if: sales_tax_assessment_appeal and agreement_precedes_completion and construction_for_purchaser and consideration_for_construction and termination_clause_exists and not (agreement_terminated and unit_retained_by_developer)

issues.definition: For a qualifying pre-completion construction agreement, a termination clause does not remove its works-contract character unless the agreement is terminated and the developer retains the unit.
